RFC 7322 — RFC Style Guide (digest)
This document describes the fundamental and unique style conventions
and editing requirements for RFCs.

Structure:
- An RFC is a complete, individually reviewable document with a fixed
  structure: front matter (title, authors, status), body, and
  back matter (references, appendices).
- The title should be descriptive, specific, and as neutral as
  possible; at most 42 characters is recommended.
- The Status of This Memo section states the document's status
  (Standards Track, Informational, Experimental, Best Current
  Practice).
- Sections are numbered; the Abstract appears before the Introduction
  and is limited to approximately 20 lines.
- The Introduction must set the context, motivation, and scope.

Language and style:
- Use 'must', 'may', 'should' per RFC 2119 semantics only when
  normative.
- Aim for complete, unambiguous sentences; avoid ambiguity and
  unnecessary words.
- Third person and the passive voice are commonly used, but clarity
  wins.
- Abbreviations and acronyms are expanded on first use.
- Citations use the traditional RFC reference format with authors,
  title, and RFC number.

Process requirements:
- RFCs are published by the RFC Editor and go through the IETF
  stream's process; errata are tracked separately.
